questions.q: Divide $x^3+2x^2-5x+3$ by $x-2$, stating the quotient and remainder.
questions.answer: Using synthetic division with root $2$ on coefficients $1,2,-5,3$: bring down $1$; $1(2)+2=4$; $4(2)-5=3$; $3(2)+3=9$. Quotient: $x^2+4x+3$; remainder: $9$.

questions.q: Divide $2x^3-3x^2+4x-1$ by $x+1$, stating the quotient and remainder.
questions.answer: Using synthetic division with root $-1$ on coefficients $2,-3,4,-1$: bring down $2$; $2(-1)-3=-5$; $-5(-1)+4=9$; $9(-1)-1=-10$. Quotient: $2x^2-5x+9$; remainder: $-10$.

questions.q: Divide $x^4-1$ by $x^2+1$, stating the quotient and remainder.
questions.answer: Since $x^4-1=(x^2-1)(x^2+1)$ exactly (difference of squares), dividing by $x^2+1$ gives quotient $x^2-1$ and remainder $0$.

questions.q: Divide $3x^3+5x^2-2x+7$ by $x+2$, stating the quotient and remainder.
questions.answer: Using synthetic division with root $-2$ on coefficients $3,5,-2,7$: bring down $3$; $3(-2)+5=-1$; $-1(-2)-2=0$; $0(-2)+7=7$. Quotient: $3x^2-x$; remainder: $7$.

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{7x-4}{(x-1)(x+3)}$ in partial fractions.
questions.answer: $7x-4=A(x+3)+B(x-1)$. At $x=1$: $3=4A\Rightarrow A=\dfrac{3}{4}$. At $x=-3$: $-25=-4B\Rightarrow B=\dfrac{25}{4}$. Result: $\dfrac{3}{4(x-1)}+\dfrac{25}{4(x+3)}$.

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{2x+5}{x(x+5)}$ in partial fractions.
questions.answer: $2x+5=A(x+5)+Bx$. At $x=0$: $5=5A\Rightarrow A=1$. At $x=-5$: $-5=-5B\Rightarrow B=1$. Result: $\dfrac{1}{x}+\dfrac{1}{x+5}$.

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{9-x}{(x+2)(x-4)}$ in partial fractions.
questions.answer: $9-x=A(x-4)+B(x+2)$. At $x=-2$: $11=-6A\Rightarrow A=-\dfrac{11}{6}$. At $x=4$: $5=6B\Rightarrow B=\dfrac{5}{6}$. Result: $-\dfrac{11}{6(x+2)}+\dfrac{5}{6(x-4)}$.

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{4x-1}{(x-2)(x+1)}$ in partial fractions.
questions.answer: $4x-1=A(x+1)+B(x-2)$. At $x=2$: $7=3A\Rightarrow A=\dfrac{7}{3}$. At $x=-1$: $-5=-3B\Rightarrow B=\dfrac{5}{3}$. Result: $\dfrac{7}{3(x-2)}+\dfrac{5}{3(x+1)}$.

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{3x+2}{(x+2)^2}$ in partial fractions of the form $\dfrac{A}{x+2}+\dfrac{B}{(x+2)^2}$.
questions.answer: $3x+2=A(x+2)+B$. At $x=-2$: $-4=B$. Comparing $x$ coefficients: $A=3$. Result: $\dfrac{3}{x+2}-\dfrac{4}{(x+2)^2}$.

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{x-4}{(x-1)^2}$ in partial fractions of the form $\dfrac{A}{x-1}+\dfrac{B}{(x-1)^2}$.
questions.answer: $x-4=A(x-1)+B$. At $x=1$: $-3=B$. Comparing $x$ coefficients: $A=1$. Result: $\dfrac{1}{x-1}-\dfrac{3}{(x-1)^2}$.

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{2x+3}{(x-3)^2}$ in partial fractions of the form $\dfrac{A}{x-3}+\dfrac{B}{(x-3)^2}$.
questions.answer: $2x+3=A(x-3)+B$. At $x=3$: $9=B$. Comparing $x$ coefficients: $A=2$. Result: $\dfrac{2}{x-3}+\dfrac{9}{(x-3)^2}$.

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{5x^2-4x-1}{x(x-1)^2}$ in partial fractions of the form $\dfrac{A}{x}+\dfrac{B}{x-1}+\dfrac{C}{(x-1)^2}$.
questions.answer: $5x^2-4x-1=A(x-1)^2+Bx(x-1)+Cx$. At $x=0$: $-1=A\Rightarrow A=-1$. At $x=1$: $0=C\Rightarrow C=0$. Comparing $x^2$ coefficients: $5=A+B\Rightarrow B=6$. Result: $-\dfrac{1}{x}+\dfrac{6}{x-1}$.

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{4x^2-x+3}{(x-2)(x^2+1)}$ in partial fractions of the form $\dfrac{A}{x-2}+\dfrac{Bx+C}{x^2+1}$.
questions.answer: $4x^2-x+3=A(x^2+1)+(Bx+C)(x-2)$. At $x=2$: $17=5A\Rightarrow A=\dfrac{17}{5}$. Comparing $x^2$ coefficients: $4=A+B\Rightarrow B=\dfrac{3}{5}$. Comparing constants: $3=A-2C\Rightarrow C=\dfrac{1}{5}$. Result: $\dfrac{17}{5(x-2)}+\dfrac{3x+1}{5(x^2+1)}$.

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{2x^2+3}{(x+1)(x^2+2)}$ in partial fractions of the form $\dfrac{A}{x+1}+\dfrac{Bx+C}{x^2+2}$.
questions.answer: $2x^2+3=A(x^2+2)+(Bx+C)(x+1)$. At $x=-1$: $5=3A\Rightarrow A=\dfrac{5}{3}$. Comparing $x^2$ coefficients: $2=A+B\Rightarrow B=\dfrac{1}{3}$. Comparing constants: $3=2A+C\Rightarrow C=-\dfrac{1}{3}$. Result: $\dfrac{5}{3(x+1)}+\dfrac{x-1}{3(x^2+2)}$.

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{x^2+2}{(x+2)(x^2+4)}$ in partial fractions of the form $\dfrac{A}{x+2}+\dfrac{Bx+C}{x^2+4}$.
questions.answer: $x^2+2=A(x^2+4)+(Bx+C)(x+2)$. At $x=-2$: $6=8A\Rightarrow A=\dfrac{3}{4}$. Comparing $x^2$ coefficients: $1=A+B\Rightarrow B=\dfrac{1}{4}$. Comparing constants: $2=4A+2C\Rightarrow C=-\dfrac{1}{2}$. Result: $\dfrac{3}{4(x+2)}+\dfrac{x-2}{4(x^2+4)}$.

sections.heading: Improper fractions: combining division with partial fractions

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{x^3+1}{x^2-1}$ as a polynomial plus a proper fraction, simplifying fully.
questions.answer: Dividing: $x^3+1=x(x^2-1)+(x+1)$, so $\dfrac{x^3+1}{x^2-1}=x+\dfrac{x+1}{x^2-1}$. Since $x^2-1=(x-1)(x+1)$, the fraction simplifies: $\dfrac{x+1}{(x-1)(x+1)}=\dfrac{1}{x-1}$ (for $x\neq-1$). Result: $x+\dfrac{1}{x-1}$.

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{x^2+3x+1}{x+1}$ as a polynomial plus a proper fraction, using division.
questions.answer: Dividing: $x^2+3x+1=(x+1)(x+2)-1$. Result: $x+2-\dfrac{1}{x+1}$.

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{2x^3-x^2+3}{x^2-1}$ as a polynomial plus a proper fraction, simplifying fully.
Express $\dfrac{x^2+5x+2}{x+3}$ as a polynomial plus a proper fraction, using division.
questions.answer: Dividing: $x^2+5x+2=(x+3)(x+2)-4$. Result: $x+2-\dfrac{4}{x+3}$.

questions.q: Use the cover-up method to express $\dfrac{5x^2+x-2}{(x-1)(x+2)(x-4)}$ in partial fractions.
Use the cover-up method to express $\dfrac{7x-3}{x(x-1)(x+3)}$ in partial fractions.
Use the cover-up method to express $\dfrac{3x+5}{(x+1)(x-2)}$ in partial fractions.

sections.heading: Using partial fractions for series expansion

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{3}{(1-x)(1+2x)}$ in partial fractions, then write the first three terms of its series expansion in ascending powers of $x$.
questions.answer: $3=A(1+2x)+B(1-x)$. At $x=1$: $A=1$. At $x=-\dfrac{1}{2}$: $B=2$. Result: $\dfrac{1}{1-x}+\dfrac{2}{1+2x}$. Expanding each geometric series: $(1+x+x^2+\cdots)+2(1-2x+4x^2-\cdots)=3-3x+9x^2+\cdots$.

questions.q: Express $\dfrac{2}{(1+x)(1-2x)}$ in partial fractions, then find the coefficient of $x^2$ in its series expansion in ascending powers of $x$.
questions.answer: $2=A(1-2x)+B(1+x)$. At $x=-1$: $A=\dfrac{2}{3}$. At $x=\dfrac{1}{2}$: $B=\dfrac{4}{3}$. Result: $\dfrac{2/3}{1+x}+\dfrac{4/3}{1-2x}$. Expanding: $\dfrac{2}{3}(1-x+x^2-\cdots)+\dfrac{4}{3}(1+2x+4x^2+\cdots)$. Coefficient of $x^2$: $\dfrac{2}{3}(1)+\dfrac{4}{3}(4)=\dfrac{2}{3}+\dfrac{16}{3}=6$.

questions.q: Given $\dfrac{2x+1}{(x+1)(x+3)}\equiv\dfrac{A}{x+1}+\dfrac{B}{x+3}$, find $A$ and $B$ by equating coefficients, and verify using $x=0$.
questions.answer: $2x+1=A(x+3)+B(x+1)=(A+B)x+(3A+B)$. Equating: $A+B=2$ and $3A+B=1$. Subtracting: $2A=-1\Rightarrow A=-\dfrac{1}{2}$, so $B=\dfrac{5}{2}$. Verify at $x=0$: LHS $=\dfrac{1}{3}$; RHS $=-\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{5}{6}=\dfrac{1}{3}$ ✓.

questions.q: Given $\dfrac{x+7}{x^2-x-6}\equiv\dfrac{A}{x-3}+\dfrac{B}{x+2}$, find $A$ and $B$ by equating coefficients, and verify using $x=1$.
questions.answer: Factoring $x^2-x-6=(x-3)(x+2)$: $x+7=A(x+2)+B(x-3)=(A+B)x+(2A-3B)$. Equating: $A+B=1$ and $2A-3B=7$. Substituting $B=1-A$: $2A-3(1-A)=7\Rightarrow5A=10\Rightarrow A=2$, so $B=-1$. Verify at $x=1$: LHS $=\dfrac{8}{-6}=-\dfrac{4}{3}$; RHS $=\dfrac{2}{-2}-\dfrac{1}{3}=-\dfrac{4}{3}$ ✓.

questions.q: Given $\dfrac{x-1}{(x+2)(x-3)}\equiv\dfrac{A}{x+2}+\dfrac{B}{x-3}$, find $A$ and $B$ by equating coefficients, and verify using $x=0$.
questions.answer: $x-1=A(x-3)+B(x+2)=(A+B)x+(-3A+2B)$. Equating: $A+B=1$ and $-3A+2B=-1$. Substituting $B=1-A$: $-3A+2(1-A)=-1\Rightarrow-5A=-3\Rightarrow A=\dfrac{3}{5}$, so $B=\dfrac{2}{5}$. Verify at $x=0$: LHS $=\dfrac{-1}{(2)(-3)}=\dfrac{1}{6}$; RHS $=\dfrac{3/5}{2}+\dfrac{2/5}{-3}=\dfrac{3}{10}-\dfrac{2}{15}=\dfrac{9}{30}-\dfrac{4}{30}=\dfrac{5}{30}=\dfrac{1}{6}$ ✓.

sections.heading: A well-designed word problem: an electrical transfer function

questions.q: This question has three parts. An engineer analyzes a circuit with transfer function $H(s)=\dfrac{5s+7}{(s+1)(s+2)}$. (a) Express $H(s)$ in partial fractions. (b) Find $H(0)$ directly from the original expression, and verify it matches the value from your decomposition. (c) A modified circuit has transfer function $\dfrac{5s^2+12s+9}{(s+1)(s+2)}$. Using polynomial division, express this in the form (constant) + (partial fractions).
questions.answer: (a) $5s+7=A(s+2)+B(s+1)$. At $s=-1$: $A=2$. At $s=-2$: $B=3$. So $H(s)=\dfrac{2}{s+1}+\dfrac{3}{s+2}$. (b) $H(0)=\dfrac{7}{(1)(2)}=3.5$. Decomposition at $s=0$: $\dfrac{2}{1}+\dfrac{3}{2}=3.5$ ✓, confirming a match. (c) Since $(s+1)(s+2)=s^2+3s+2$ has the same degree as the numerator, divide first: $5s^2+12s+9=5(s^2+3s+2)+(-3s-1)$, so the expression equals $5-\dfrac{3s+1}{(s+1)(s+2)}$. Decomposing $\dfrac{3s+1}{(s+1)(s+2)}$: $3s+1=A(s+2)+B(s+1)$; at $s=-1$, $A=-2$; at $s=-2$, $B=5$. So $\dfrac{3s+1}{(s+1)(s+2)}=-\dfrac{2}{s+1}+\dfrac{5}{s+2}$, giving the final result $5+\dfrac{2}{s+1}-\dfrac{5}{s+2}$.
